subject: Comprehensive Zoning Ordinance Recodification
overview: The board held a public hearing on a comprehensive zoning recodification proposal to update the city's 1965 ordinance. No final decision was reached, and the hearing was continued to December 9 following extensive public testimony regarding residential occupancy limits and parking requirements.

items.title: Introduction to Zoning Recodification
items.summary: Alicia Hunt explained that the city council engaged an attorney to clean up and recodify the zoning ordinance to bring it in line with current legal statutes.

items.title: Section 1: General Provisions
items.summary: Attorney Mark Bobrowski presented section one, which establishes the authority, scope, and severability of the ordinance using boilerplate language consistent with state law.

items.title: Section 2: Establishment of Districts
items.summary: The board reviewed the establishment of districts, including a new Office 2 (O2) district for research and development, and provisions for lots split by district boundaries.

items.title: Section 3: Use Regulations and Accessory Uses
items.summary: Discussion focused on the regulation of accessory uses, including home occupations and family childcare facilities.

items.title: Public Testimony on Housing and Family Definition
items.summary: Residents and board members expressed significant concern regarding the proposed definition of a family and restrictions that would limit the number of unrelated persons and lodgers in residential dwellings.

items.title: Use Table Review
items.summary: Attorney Bobrowski reviewed the restructured use table, which includes updated categories for Dover Amendment uses, retail tiers, and new allowances for breweries and taprooms.

items.title: Section 4: Dimensional Regulations
items.summary: The board examined dimensional requirements, specifically height and lot coverage flexibility for the proposed O2 district intended to accommodate life sciences development.

items.title: Section 5: Nonconforming Uses and Structures
items.summary: The proposal introduces simplified rules for altering nonconforming single- and two-family homes, allowing certain expansions by building permit or special permit rather than variances.

items.title: Section 6: Parking and Sign Regulations
items.summary: The board reviewed new provisions for shared parking and the ability for permit-granting authorities to waive minimum parking or sign requirements via special permit.

items.title: Proposed Residential Parking Minimum Reduction
items.summary: Chair Andre Leroux proposed recommending that the city council reduce the parking requirement for multifamily residential units from 2.0 spaces to 1.25 spaces per unit.

items.title: Continuance and Administrative Updates
items.summary: The board voted to continue the hearing to December 9, 2021, and announced the hiring of a new administrative assistant.
